title: Degrees of Comparison
subtitle: Fast, faster, fastest. And when to use more.

cards.title: Three degrees, and only two of them compare
cards.text: Fast. Faster. Fastest. The first just describes; the other two measure one thing against others.

cards.title: Positive, comparative, superlative
cards.text: Each has a job, and using the wrong one is immediately noticeable.

cards.title: Count the syllables
cards.text: That is genuinely the rule, with one grey area in the middle.
points: **Three or more** → more / most: *powerful, more powerful*.
**Two syllables** → usually more/most, but -y words take -ier: *heavy, heavier*.

cards.title: How many are you comparing?
cards.text: Count first, then pick the form. The bars do the counting for you.

question.explain: One syllable takes -er, and you never use more as well.

cards.title: A spec sheet is comparisons all the way down
cards.text: Every number on it exists to be measured against another car.
points: **This one is faster than that one.** Comparative, with than.
**It is the quickest in its class.** Superlative, with the.
**More powerful**, because powerful is three syllables.

cards.title: A short list that refuses the pattern
cards.text: These are the ones worth memorising, because they are used constantly.

question.explain: Good is irregular: better. 'Gooder' is the same over-regularising as 'catched'.

cards.title: Comparing two fighters, then the whole division
cards.text: The grammar changes depending on how many you are measuring against.
points: **He is stronger than me.** Two people, comparative.
**He is the strongest in the gym.** The whole group, superlative.
**Swap those two** and the sentence stops making sense.

options: She is the best of the three.
She is the better of the three.
question.explain: Three or more means superlative: the best.

cards.title: Hot, hotter, hottest
cards.alt: Three red chillies in a row, small, medium and large
cards.text: One on its own is just hot. It takes two to be hotter and three to be hottest.

cards.title: Literature Review: Don Quixote, Chapter 17: With Friends and Neighbors
cards.text: Home at last, Quixote is fussed over by the priest and the barber. They compare him with the man he used to be.
points: **They agree the books are the worst** of his problems.

terms.def: The plain adjective, describing without comparing.
Compares two things; takes -er or more, and 'than'.
Compares three or more; takes -est or most, and 'the'.
The error of using both -er and more.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Positive describes, comparative compares two, superlative compares all.
Short words take -er/-est; long words take more/most.

quiz.text: 'More faster' is correct in informal speech.
quiz.explain: It is a double comparative and wrong in any register.

quiz.text: Comparative forms are usually followed by…
Write the comparative of 'heavy'. One word.
'She is the ____ in the whole gym.' Which fits?

options: He is more taller than me.

quiz.text: Write the superlative of 'far'. One word.
In Chapter 17, who looks after Quixote when he gets home?
options: The priest, the barber and his housekeeper
quiz.explain: They fuss over him and compare him with the man he used to be.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 7 English. The three degrees are separated by how many things are being measured, which is the distinction that actually governs the choice, and the grammatical markers are attached to each ('than' for the comparative, 'the' for the superlative) so he has a check he can apply to his own sentences. The syllable rule is given plainly because it works. Double comparatives get their own checkpoint and are linked explicitly back to over-regularising from week 2, since 'more faster' and 'catched' are the same instinct.
discussion: How do you know whether to use -er or more?
What word always follows a comparative?
extension: Compare three objects in the room using all three degrees.
Find five comparatives in a car or phone review.
misconceptions: Double comparatives: more faster, most fastest.
Using the comparative for three or more things.
